contradictions.detail: The listing's Vehicle History Report panel states 'No Accident or Damage Reported'. The AutoCheck report for the same VIN shows a 09/02/2025 minor-moderate damage event with rear damage and 'Damage or Repair to Structure Reported'.

critical_evidence.evidence: The listing is silent on track or autocross use. AutoCheck reports 6 brake pad replacements by ~47k mi and frequent early tire and suspension service under owner 1 (32k mi in ~22 months). That pattern warrants the question but does not prove track use. Oil-consumption answer and compression/leakdown not provided.

Passed CA smog 03/04/2025 at 41,078 mi under the previous owner. Exhaust tips appear stock in photos. Nothing covers the current owner's period, and 'Emission System Serviced' entries at 10/2025 and 07/2026 are unexplained. An ECU calibration ID/CVN check is needed.

The profile scopes NHTSA 21V587000 to 2018-2019 model years. This is a 2020 (in service 12/2020). AutoCheck reports 'No Open Recalls' and the tracker recall list is empty. Confirm with a Toyota VIN recall lookup at PPI.

documentation.rationale: VIN, price, and an AutoCheck with 18 service entries, title, lien and odometer data cover identity and partial maintenance. Missing: repair invoices for the 09/2025 rear structural damage, itemised service invoices, tire dates, and photos of the at-risk rear structure and underbody.

condition.rationale: Reported rear structural damage/repair (09/2025) has no repair documentation. A possible line or crack in the lower left rear bumper cover is visible. Brake service frequency is high. Panels otherwise look straight and the wheels clean, but photo backgrounds are digitally removed and the lead image appears edited.

price_value.rationale: $23,000 sits near the $23,833 fair-value midpoint. That estimate assumes no damage history, while this car carries a reported structural-damage event that typically depresses resale. It is not priced to reflect that.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual RWD, naturally aspirated FA20 and Toyota-level parts support suit the bridge brief. Price is above the $19,000 ideal band but under the $27,000 ceiling. Resale in 6-24 months will be weighed down by the reported accident.

logistics.rationale: Stockton is a short drive from Carmel and the car is CA-registered and smog-feasible. PSX escrow handles lien payoff. PPI access before payment is not stated and the seller does not hold title.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: TRD Handling Package (Sachs dampers, Brembo brakes) with a 6-speed manual is a desirable spec. Gray is common, and the reported accident and non-OE tires dilute originality.

Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, plus photos of the trunk floor with the mat lifted and the rear bumper corners?
ppi_focus: Rear structure from the 09/2025 damage: trunk floor, tail panel, rear rails, quarter-panel seams and spare well. Use a paint-depth meter and check panel gaps, and measure the frame if anything is irregular.
Lower left rear bumper cover line: check for a crack versus misfit and inspect the bumper reinforcement and mounts.
Clutch engagement point, slip test in high gear, throwout bearing noise, and shift quality.
Signs of track use: brake rotor heat checking and pad compound, tire wear pattern, scuffed underbody aero panels. Run compression/leakdown and an oil-condition check if any indicators appear.
Read ECU calibration ID/CVN against Toyota stock to rule out a current or removed tune, and check smog readiness monitors.
Full scan for stored and pending codes. Verify no fuel-pump or other open recalls via Toyota VIN lookup.
Sachs dampers for leaks, alignment readings, and steering rack (steering service reported 07/2026).
Tire date codes and matching, and wheel straightness.
Fluid condition: brake fluid, transmission and differential oil, coolant. Check for oil weeping.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a professional body-shop invoice showing a minor rear repair (bumper cover/reinforcement only) plus a clean PPI with normal paint readings and straight rear structure.
Up: a price adjustment reflecting the reported structural-damage history.
Down: evidence of rear rail, trunk-floor or tail-panel sectioning, poor repair quality, or refusal of a PPI before payment.
Down: signs of track use, an ECU tune, clutch slip, or oil consumption at inspection.
evidence.mission_note: A manual, naturally aspirated, Toyota-backed RWD coupe squarely matches the enthusiast-bridge brief and is close to Carmel. Its resale value as a 6-24 month bridge depends on what the reported 09/2025 rear structural damage actually was.
evidence.rationale: The VIN, CA clean title (with active lien) and a consistent odometer are established by the AutoCheck, which also shows three owners and 18 service entries, including regular oil and coolant service through 07/2026. The same report records a 09/02/2025 minor-moderate rear damage event flagged 'Damage or Repair to Structure Reported'. This directly contradicts the listing's 'No Accident or Damage Reported' panel, and no repair documentation is supplied. The photos show the TRD Handling Package hardware and stock-looking exhaust and wheels, plus Cooper tires of unknown date and a possible line or crack in the lower left rear bumper cover in the damage zone. The history also shows six brake pad replacements by ~47k miles and no reported service entries from 10/2021 to 03/2024. Track use, tune status since the 03/2025 smog pass, clutch condition and PPI access before payment remain open. At $23,000 the asking price sits at the no-accident fair-value midpoint despite the reported structural event.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller asking for the 09/2025 body-shop invoice and photos of the trunk floor and rear structure, and written confirmation that an independent PPI can happen before any PSX payment.
